prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key proposals in the Conservative Party Manifesto 2024 (ideological framing removed)

- Economy and tax
  - Cut employee National Insurance to 6% by April 2027; abolish main rate of self‑employed NI by end of Parliament.
  - “Triple Lock Plus” so the State Pension and a new age-related personal allowance both rise by the highest of earnings, inflation or 2.5%.
  - Maintain rates of income tax, VAT and corporation tax; maintain National Living Wage at two‑thirds of median earnings.
  - Raise at least £6bn/year by tackling tax avoidance/evasion.

- Families, childcare and welfare
  - 30 hours’ free childcare from nine months to school start by Sept 2025.
  - Move Child Benefit to a household test: taper from £120k to £160k household income.
  - Welfare reform: redesign PIP and work capability assessments; shift fit notes to specialist services; tougher sanctions after 12 months; Fraud Bill; complete Universal Credit rollout.

- Business, SMEs and regulation
  - Maintain full expensing and consider extending to leasing; no rise in corporation tax.
  - SME 10‑point plan (business rates relief, VAT threshold reform options, prompt payment enforcement, access to finance, capital rules, female/disabled entrepreneurship support).

- Infrastructure, digital and transport
  - Reallocate HS2 savings to regional schemes; £8.3bn for potholes; Northern Powerhouse Rail (Manchester–Liverpool), Midlands Rail Hub; electrify North Wales Main Line.
  - Gigabit nationwide by 2030; standalone 5G in all populated areas.
  - Backing Drivers Bill: ban local road pricing, require referendums for new LTNs/20mph; reverse London ULEZ expansion.
  - Rail Reform Bill to create Great British Railways; national contactless pay‑as‑you‑go; extend £2 bus fare cap for the Parliament.

- Innovation, industry and trade
  - Public R&D to £22bn/year; £1.5bn for AI compute; £4.5bn Advanced Manufacturing Plan; expand Catapults.
  - Complete FTAs with India and GCC; implement CPTPP; no changes to NHS or UK food standards in trade deals.

- Government efficiency
  - Reduce civil service to pre‑pandemic size; halve consultancy spend; move 25k roles out of London; double digital/AI expertise; 2% annual productivity plans.

- Education and skills
  - Advanced British Standard for 16–19; two hours’ PE weekly; mobile phone bans in schools; register for children not in school.
  - 100,000 more apprenticeships funded by closing low‑outcome university courses; Lifelong Learning Entitlement.
  - Mandatory National Service at 18: paid competitive military/cyber placements or part‑time civic service.

- Borders and migration
  - Legal annual cap on work/family visas, falling each year; health checks and higher fees/IHS where applicable.
  - Rwanda removals; implement Illegal Migration Act; more returns deals; seek reforms to international asylum rules.

- Defence and foreign policy
  - Defence spending to 2.5% of GDP by 2030; at least £10bn for munitions; defence R&D min 5% plus 2% for exploitation.
  - Long‑term support for Ukraine; National Defence and Resilience Plan.
  - Veterans Bill; maintain Office for Veterans’ Affairs.

- Health and social care
  - Real‑terms NHS funding growth; 92,000 more nurses and 28,000 more doctors; expand Pharmacy First; 250 GP surgeries; 50 more Community Diagnostic Centres; 40 hospitals by 2030.
  - Dental Recovery Plan, contractual reform, NHS service requirement for new dentists.
  - £3.4bn for NHS tech (NHS App as single front door, AI diagnostics); reduce 5,500 managers; Major Conditions Strategy; Tobacco and Vapes Bill; maternity and women’s health actions; implement Cass Review.

- Energy, climate and environment
  - Annual North Sea licensing; new gas power stations; treble offshore wind; deliver CCUS clusters; approve two SMR fleets within 100 days; new plant at Wylfa; import carbon pricing by 2027.
  - No new green levies; maintain price cap; £6bn for home efficiency and a universal voucher scheme; onshore wind with local consent; protect best farmland from solar; retain fracking moratorium.
  - Plan for Water enforcement, tougher penalties, river recovery network; tree/peatland programmes; new National Park; deposit return scheme; restrict new incinerators.

- Housing and planning
  - 1.6m homes; lift “nutrient neutrality” block with mitigation fees; fast‑track brownfield in 20 largest cities; urban regeneration corporations.
  - Permanent FTB SDLT threshold £425k; new Help to Buy; Mortgage Guarantee continuation.
  - Leasehold reform (cap ground rents, end misuse of forfeiture); Renters Reform (abolish Section 21 after court reforms); temporary CGT relief for landlords selling to tenants; local/UK connection tests for social housing.

- Communities, agriculture, fisheries and devolution
  - £20m endowments for 105 towns; extend Community Ownership Fund and UK Shared Prosperity Fund; more Freeports/Investment Zones.
  - Farming budget +£1bn over Parliament (inflation‑linked); legal food security target and index; fast‑track farm infrastructure; five‑year tapered seasonal visas; replicate £100m Seafood Fund.
  - Continue UK‑wide investments; comparable public‑service performance data; implement Windsor Framework and Safeguarding the Union measures.
